ut_long_canyon.blurb: Long Canyon sits along Potash Road, about half an hour from Moab in southeast Utah. It is a sandstone trad destination: nearly everything here is crack climbing, from thin tips through hands to offwidths, on solid Wingate stone, with only a few sport routes and boulder problems. Grades run from the 5.8 range up to 5.12, and the bulk fall between 5.10 and 5.12. The walls are scattered through the canyon rather than packed into one spot. Maverick Buttress holds the most routes and has the easiest walk in; it faces east, so it gets morning sun and afternoon shade. The Shipyard is the other main cluster and gets more sun. Reptilian Wall and Deadman's Buttress add more trad. Some of the less-traveled lines have loose rock.

wv_snake_hill_wildlife_management_area.blurb: Snake Hill is a state-managed tract of rolling highlands and steep slopes on the south side of the Cheat River canyon in northern West Virginia, across the gorge from Coopers Rock. The rock is sandstone, and bouldering makes up most of the climbing, with roped sport and trad alongside it and a few top-rope lines. Problems start at the easiest grades and reach V10, with the greatest number between V0 and V3 and a solid group of harder ones. Roped climbs span roughly 5.7 to 5.13. First Bell Boulders and Junction Boulders are the biggest boulder clusters, Hole N The Wall is the main sport wall, and Snowflake Wall and the Trad Wall area hold the traditional lines. This is lesser-explored sandstone.

az_waterfall_the_2.blurb: The Waterfall is a broad amphitheater of columnar basalt on the east side of Oak Creek Canyon, a few miles north of Sedona. The climbing is hard single-pitch trad: splitter cracks, gear-protected faces and some mixed lines with a few bolts, and very few pure sport routes. Nothing here is easy. Grades start at a solid 5.10, most routes fall in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, and there are a number of 5.13 lines on top. The walls face different ways. The Left Wall looks east and gets morning light, the Right Wall faces west and is shaded early, and the Double Clutching Wall faces south and gets the most sun. The Main Amphitheater faces south but the rim holds off the sun until midday. Many pitches start on blocky rock, and rockfall is a concern, so a helmet at the base is wise.

ar_richland_creek_area.blurb: Richland Creek is a large, backcountry-feeling climbing area in north-central Arkansas, with plenty of room for both boulders and roped lines. Sport and trad are close to evenly split, with a boulder contingent on top. Roped grades run from the 5.4 range to 5.13, with the most weight at 5.10 and below, so moderates are well served; boulder problems run from V2 to V9. Stack Rock holds the most routes: a remote, secluded formation that wraps around on itself, with walls and features uncommon elsewhere in the state. Its climbing is mostly moderate and crowds are light, and depending on the wall you can find shade or sun all day. Some of its steeper features stay dry in light rain. Heaven Boulders is the bouldering cluster, and Horn Mountain and Prohibition add more roped climbing.

ca_fresno_dome_wamello_area.blurb: The Fresno Dome area is on the western slope of the southern Sierra Nevada, in Sierra National Forest above Oakhurst and Bass Lake. The rock is Sierra granite: smooth slabs, steeper faces, knobs and some cracks. The dome itself is mostly multi-pitch trad, usually three to five pitches, and some older lines can feel run out by modern standards. Across the whole area sport routes outnumber trad, with shorter bolted climbs at places like Willow Creek Wall. Grades run from the 5.7 range to 5.12, with most climbs around 5.10 and a good number at 5.11 and below that at 5.8 and 5.9. The elevation keeps summers fairly cool, and summer and fall are generally the best times to climb. Crowds are rare. Enchanted Rock adds more sport.

ca_mountaineer_walls.blurb: Mountaineer Walls is a spread of cliffs on El Cajon Mountain in San Diego County, arranged as a series of tiers (first, second, third and west) plus named walls such as the Toe, Bastion and Chocolate Wall. Sport routes lead, with trad a solid second. Grades run from the 5.5 range to 5.12, centered on 5.10 with a fair number of 5.8 and 5.9. The rock offers slabs, corners, arêtes, faces, cracks and a few steep overhangs, and it is an acquired taste, with dirt, grass and loose rock in places. The Toe is a large wall: granite, mostly moderate climbing, facing south, which makes it a good winter choice. Several crags get afternoon shade, and the area suits cooler days better than hot ones.
